title: Check If N and Its Double Exist
spaceBreakdown:
- bool seen[4001]: fixed 4001 entries, independent of n → O(1)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input vector
approach: Since arr[i] is bounded to [−10³, 10³], the value 2·arr[j] can only lie in [−2000, 2000] - a fixed range of 4001 integers. We use a direct-address boolean table of size 4001 (offset by 2000) to record every value seen so far. For each element x we check whether 2·x or x/2 (when x is even) has already been marked; if so, a valid pair exists. This gives O(n) time with O(1) auxiliary space because the table size is constant.
hints: Given that every arr[i] lies between −10³ and 10³, how many distinct values could 2·arr[j] ever take?
Use a fixed-size boolean lookup table indexed by value (offset by 2000). For arr = [10,2,5,3], when we reach 5 we find 2·5 = 10 was already marked → true.

**Zero single occurrence** - zero is its own double, but i must differ from j.
`Input: arr = [0,1]` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: marking seen[x] before checking → returns true (same-index match on 0).

**Double appears after half** - the larger value comes later in the array.
`Input: arr = [7,14]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: only checking 2*x (never x/2) → returns false.

**Boundary value** - 2·x reaches the edge of the lookup range.
`Input: arr = [500,1000]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: sizing the table to cover only [−1000,1000] (size 2001) → index 2·1000+2000 = 4000 is out of bounds → crash.

**All equal non-zero** - duplicates exist but none is double another.
`Input: arr = [5,5]` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: returning true on any duplicate → returns true.

followUps.q: What if arr[i] could be up to 10⁹?
followUps.a: The fixed-range table no longer works because 2·x could be 2·10⁹. Replace it with an unordered_set<int> using the same single-pass logic - O(n) time, O(n) space.

followUps.q: What if you must return all valid index pairs (i, j)?
followUps.a: Store a list of indices per value in a map instead of a boolean. For each x, look up 2·x and x/2, then emit every prior index found. Time stays O(n + output size), space becomes O(n).

followUps.q: What if the array arrives as a stream and you can retain only k elements?
followUps.a: Keep a sliding window of the last k values in the lookup table, evicting the oldest as you advance. Pairs farther than k apart may be missed. Time O(n), space O(k).
